readmeHtml:
Lap - Private Local Photo Manager

Open-source desktop photo manager for macOS, Windows, and Linux.

English | Česky | Deutsch | Español | Français | Italiano | Magyar | Nederlands | Polski | Português | Русский | Українська | Tiếng Việt | 中文简体 | 中文繁體 | 日本語 | 한국어

Lap is a free, open-source, local-first photo manager for macOS, Windows, and Linux. Browse and organize your existing photo folders, search with on-device AI, and manage large libraries without a cloud account or subscription.

OFFICIAL WEBSITE | DEMO

Important

Lap’s only official website is currently julyx10.github.io/lap. lapphotos.com is not an official website, has no affiliation with the Lap project, and is neither authorized nor endorsed by the project.

Download Lap

Please download Lap directly from GitHub Releases whenever possible, rather than from third-party websites.

Platform Package Note
macOS (Apple Silicon / Intel) _aarch64.dmg / _x64.dmg Notarized by Apple
Windows 10/11 (x64 / ARM64) _x64_en-US.msi / _arm64_en-US.msi Unsigned. If your browser blocks the download, choose Keep anyway. If SmartScreen blocks the installer, choose More info → Run anyway.
Linux (x64 / ARM64) _amd64.deb / _arm64.deb For Debian-based distros (Ubuntu, Debian, Linux Mint, etc.)
Linux (x64 / ARM64) _amd64.AppImage / _aarch64.AppImage Make the file executable, then double-click to run

macOS with Homebrew

brew install --cask lap

Previously installed via the julyx10/lap tap? See the migration instructions.

Screenshots

Why Lap

  • Private, on-device AI. Search by description, find similar photos, and browse by face with processing performed locally.
  • Your folders, under your control. Open existing folders directly. Your originals stay in place, with no required upload or library import.
  • Metadata that works across apps. Read embedded EXIF/IPTC/XMP and existing sidecars, with support for saving edited metadata to XMP sidecars while leaving original files untouched.
  • Culling built for photographers. Instant Space-bar preview, auto-advance after rating, autofocus area overlay, four-pane comparison, and duplicate keep rules.
  • Built for libraries with 100,000+ photos and videos. A native Rust core powers browsing, search, and scanning.
  • Free and open source. No subscription, no account, no forced ecosystem. 17 languages, on macOS, Windows, and Linux.

Features

  • Flexible library browsing by date, folder, location, camera, lens, tags, ratings, and faces, with sorting and search.
  • Folder-first workflow with multiple libraries, drag-&-drop import/export, copy-paste import/export, batch rename, filesystem sync, and safe move/copy/delete operations.
  • Local AI search for text prompts, visual similarity, subjects, face clustering, and optional multilingual search in 50+ languages.
  • Metadata import and XMP writeback: read embedded EXIF/IPTC/XMP and sidecars (ratings, tags, favorites, culling flags, GPS, dates, and more), edit text fields, and write your organization back to XMP sidecars.
  • Smart Albums save rule-based views with custom grouping, sorting, folder-name filters, and searchable value pickers.
  • Date-organized import with day, month, year, or single-folder layouts, original filenames, and duplicate skipping.
  • Collections and hierarchical tags to organize files in bulk, with a drag-to-reorder tag tree and subtree counts.
  • Duplicate cleanup with keep rules (preferred folders, format, size, date), reclaimable-space summaries, and bulk removal.
  • Culling and comparison tools including a four-pane comparison viewer and auto-advance.
  • Built-in editing for crop, arbitrary-angle straighten, rotate, flip, resize, and basic image adjustments.
  • Photo Collage to compose selected photos into grid, justified-mosaic, or picture-pile layouts.
  • Apple Live Photos and Google Motion Photos with motion playback and a unified Smart Album filter.
  • RAW + JPEG/HEIC pairs displayed as one item and kept together during file operations, with a choice of deletion scope.
  • Configurable RAW thumbnails and previews using RAW rendering or the camera's embedded preview, with adjustable brightness and RAW+JPEG pair display.
  • Customizable File Info with selectable fields, lazy-loaded details, and an autofocus area overlay in the viewer.
  • Interactive Map View to explore geotagged photos and videos in clusters that follow your current filters.
  • Offline album browsing that keeps albums on disconnected or network storage visible with cached thumbnails.
  • Cloud-only file browsing for OneDrive Files On-Demand and macOS dataless files: indexed and shown without downloading. Lap never downloads them automatically.
  • Light and dark themes, optionally following the system appearance.
  • Broad format support for 60+ image, RAW, and video formats, plus Affinity document previews.

Metadata and Data Ownership

Lap is folder-first. Most of the information shown in Lap is read from your files, and you can choose to write your organization back to standard XMP sidecars so it travels with the files and stays readable by other photo apps.

Lap imports compatible metadata from Lightroom, digiKam, darktable, and ACDSee. Supported fields vary by application.

Read existing metadata

  • Your original photos and videos always remain ordinary files in their existing folders.
  • Embedded EXIF, IPTC, and XMP metadata is read when Lap indexes the file: capture date, camera, lens, GPS, orientation, ratings, favorites, keywords, culling flags, descriptions, title, headline, creator, copyright. Turn on Settings → Metadata → Import metadata to import the organization fields into the local database; your local edits are preserved.
  • When Lap imports metadata from an XMP sidecar, supported sidecar values take precedence over embedded values, including GPS and capture dates.

Save supported edits to XMP

  • Title, headline, description, creator, and copyright are editable in Lap. Edits are saved to the local database.
  • Save Metadata to XMP writes tags (including hierarchical keywords), ratings, favorites, culling states, title, headline, description, creator, and copyright to sidecars. It preserves unrelated XMP properties and leaves the original files untouched.
  • When you rename, move, copy, delete, or import files in Lap, Lap updates its local database and keeps XMP sidecars and supported grouped assets — Apple Live Photo components, AAE sidecars, and enabled RAW + JPEG/HEIC pairs — together with the files. When deleting a RAW pair, you can delete either file or both. The shared XMP sidecar stays with the remaining file if you keep one.
  • Saving a built-in image edit writes the resulting image to the selected destination.

What stays in Lap’s database

The following are Lap library data. They are stored in Lap's local database or library configuration:

  • Collections, Smart Albums and their rules, grouping, sorting, and ordering
  • AI search data, face data, thumbnails, and other index/cache data
  • Tags, ratings, favorites, culling states (picks and rejects), and editable text fields are stored in the local database and can be written to XMP as described above.

Edits stay in Lap’s database until you choose Save Metadata to XMP for the supported fields. Collections, Smart Albums, AI search data, and face data remain local to Lap and are not included in XMP sidecars. Back up your database to preserve this organization; copying your original files alone does not preserve it.

Working with files outside Lap

Lap can rescan folders and detect many filesystem changes. With metadata import enabled, it also checks for changes to XMP sidecars. But changes made outside Lap—such as renaming, moving, replacing, or copying files—can disrupt organization that is stored only in Lap.

Rename and move files in Lap to preserve their data in the local database, including collection membership. To share supported metadata with other apps, use Save Metadata to XMP and keep the sidecar with the file. If you also manage files outside Lap, back up Lap's database and configuration together with your photos. You can manage the database location and create a backup in Settings → Storage.

Deleting Lap's database or configuration removes this local organization and index data, but does not delete your original media files.

Uninstall Lap

Lap works directly with your existing photo folders. Uninstalling Lap, or deleting its database and cache files, does not delete your original photos.

The standard uninstall steps remove the application. To remove Lap completely, quit Lap first, uninstall the application, then delete its local database, thumbnail cache, and configuration files using the cleanup command for your platform.

macOS

If you installed Lap with Homebrew:

brew uninstall --cask lap

For a manual installation, quit Lap and move Lap.app from the Applications folder to the Trash.

To remove all Lap database, cache, and configuration files:

rm -rf "$HOME/Library/Application Support/com.julyx10.lap" \
       "$HOME/Library/Caches/com.julyx10.lap" \
       "$HOME/Library/WebKit/com.julyx10.lap"
rm -f "$HOME/Library/Preferences/com.julyx10.lap.plist"

Windows

Open Settings > Apps > Installed apps, find Lap, and select Uninstall.

Then open PowerShell and remove all Lap database, cache, and configuration files:

Remove-Item -Recurse -Force -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue "$env:LOCALAPPDATA\com.julyx10.lap"
Remove-Item -Recurse -Force -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue "$env:APPDATA\com.julyx10.lap"

Linux

For DEB installations, uninstall the package:

sudo apt remove lap

For a locally installed Arch package, use sudo pacman -R lap.

For AppImage installations, quit Lap and delete the downloaded .AppImage file.

Then remove all Lap database, cache, and configuration files:

rm -rf "$HOME/.local/share/com.julyx10.lap" \
       "$HOME/.cache/com.julyx10.lap" \
       "$HOME/.config/com.julyx10.lap"

If you selected a custom database storage directory in Lap settings, delete that directory separately after confirming that it contains only Lap database files.

Build from Source

Requirements: Node.js 20+, pnpm, Rust stable.

# macOS system deps
xcode-select --install
brew install nasm pkg-config autoconf automake libtool cmake

# Linux system deps
# sudo apt install libwebkit2gtk-4.1-dev libappindicator3-dev librsvg2-dev \
#   patchelf nasm clang pkg-config autoconf automake libtool cmake

# Clone and build
git clone --recursive https://github.com/julyx10/lap.git
cd lap
git submodule update --init --recursive
cargo install tauri-cli --version "^2.0.0" --locked
./scripts/download_models.sh            # Windows: .\scripts\download_models.ps1
./scripts/download_ffmpeg_sidecar.sh    # Windows: .\scripts\download_ffmpeg_sidecar.ps1
cd src-vite && pnpm install && cd ..
cargo tauri dev

Distribution packages can link against the system libheif (1.17 or newer) instead of the bundled libheif and libde265. Set LAP_SYSTEM_LIBHEIF=1 for the build. The submodules third_party/libheif and third_party/libde265 are then not needed. HEVC decoding depends on the codec plugins of the system libheif.

Arch Linux (x86_64)

An experimental source-built Arch recipe is in contrib/aur. It has not been published to the AUR, so yay -S lap is not available yet. To build and install it locally on Arch Linux:

cd contrib/aur
makepkg -s
sudo pacman -U lap-<version>-x86_64.pkg.tar.zst

The recipe pins an upstream source commit and checksums the bundled AI models and FFmpeg tools. The Arch build disables in-app self-updates so pacman remains responsible for upgrades; other platform builds keep their existing updater. See the recipe guide for build details and outstanding release checks.

Supported Formats

Lap supports 60+ image, RAW, and video formats.

Type Formats
Images JPG/JPEG/JFIF, PNG, GIF, BMP, TIFF, WebP, HEIC/HEIF/HIF, AVIF, JXL, PSD, EXR, HDR/RGBE, TGA, JPEG 2000 (JP2/J2K/J2C/JPC/JPF/JPX), DDS, DPX, QOI
RAW photos CR2, CR3, CRW, NEF, NRW, ARW, SRF, SR2, RAF, RW2, ORF, PEF, DNG, SRW, RWL, MRW, 3FR, MOS, IIQ, DCR, KDC, ERF, MEF, RAW, MDC
Affinity documents AF, AFPHOTO, AFDESIGN, AFPUB (embedded preview)
Videos MP4, MOV, M4V, MKV, AVI, FLV, TS/MTS/M2TS, WMV, WebM, 3GP, MPG/MPEG, VOB, MOD/TOD, HEVC, ASF. H.264 playback is supported on all platforms, with automatic compatibility processing when native playback is unavailable. HEVC/H.265 and VP9 are natively supported on macOS.

Linux Video Playback

If videos don't play, install the GStreamer plugins:

sudo apt install gstreamer1.0-libav gstreamer1.0-plugins-good

Architecture

  • Core: Tauri + Rust
  • Frontend: Vue + Vite + Tailwind CSS
  • Data: SQLite

Key Libraries

Library Purpose
LibRaw RAW image decoding and thumbnail extraction
libheif HEIC/HEIF/HIF image decoding and preview generation
libjpeg-turbo Fast JPEG decoding and thumbnail generation
FFmpeg Video processing and thumbnail generation
exiftool-rs Rust port of ExifTool
Video.js Cross-platform video playback UI
ONNX Runtime Local AI model inference engine
CLIP Image-text similarity search
InsightFace Face detection and recognition
Leaflet Interactive map for geotagged photos
daisyUI UI component library

License

GPL-3.0-or-later. See LICENSE.

Privacy

Read the Privacy Policy for details on data handling and optional online services.

releases.name: v0.4.1
releases.body:
v0.4.1 is a hotfix for a crash on macOS: opening or switching videos in Preview could close the app unexpectedly, especially in folders that mix photos and videos. The crash is fixed in this release. It also adds customizable status bar fields and fixes a Linux window issue.

## Highlights

- **macOS video crash fixed** — Lap no longer quits while you open a video in Preview or move between clips with the arrow keys. Photo-only folders were never affected. (#558)
- **Customizable status bar** — Choose which fields the status bar shows, including name and size, dimensions, folder, album, color information, capture date, camera, lens, exposure, and location. (#460)

## New Features and Improvements

- Status bar fields can be shown, hidden, and reordered from a dialog that also opens by right-clicking the status bar; Settings has an entry point for the same dialog. (#460)
- Reordering smart albums and collections moved into each panel's menu, keeping the rows themselves uncluttered.
- Cleaning unused thumbnail cache moved from the library manager to **Settings → Storage**, where it can clean all listed libraries in one pass.

releases.name: v0.4.0
releases.body:
v0.4.0 is about metadata and organization: EXIF / IPTC / XMP import and XMP writeback, a tag tree, RAW pairs handled as single items, keep rules for the duplicate finder, batch rename, and a new File Info panel. Large libraries browse faster, cloud-only files work without downloading, and there are two new languages (17 total).

## Highlights

- **Metadata (EXIF / IPTC / XMP)** — Lap reads embedded metadata via exiftool-rs and imports XMP sidecars: ratings, favorites, tags, culling flags, GPS, capture dates, and text fields (title, headline, description, creator, copyright). Sidecar values take precedence over embedded ones, and local edits are preserved. The text fields are editable in Lap, and "Save Metadata to XMP" writes them along with tags, ratings, favorites, and culling states back to sidecars without touching unrelated properties. Sidecars follow files through rename, move, copy, delete, and import. (#7, #40, #244, #282, #341, #379, #402, #439)
- **Hierarchical tags** — Tags moved from groups into a tree. Drag to reorder or reparent subtrees, search and count including descendants, edit inline. The list is virtualized and has a selected-only filter. Deleted tags stay

releases.name: v0.3.3
releases.body:
Lap v0.3.3 adds Photo Collage, tag groups, offline album browsing, and arbitrary-angle straightening. It also brings more RAW preview controls, faster startup and RAW browsing, simpler view switching and multi-select, and six new languages.

##  Highlights

- **Photo Collage** — Compose selected photos into a single shareable image with grid, justified-mosaic, and Picasa-style picture-pile layouts. Move, layer, rotate, and scale photos on the pile, randomize a layout, then export at full resolution from the originals or print to A4 or photo paper at 300 dpi, with customizable page size, orientation, background, spacing, borders, and optional drop shadows. (#358, #387)
- **Tag Groups** — Organize tags into collapsible, reorderable groups with inline editors for creating tags and groups, move tags between groups, and show the group name in content titles. A protected Default group keeps every tag categorized. (#304)

releases.name: v0.3.2
releases.body:
Lap v0.3.2 brings new ways to explore, import, and organize your photo library. Discover geotagged photos in Map View, play Google Motion Photos, import media into date-based folders, and clean up duplicates across the library. This release also adds sharper thumbnails for large displays, configurable RAW previews, and important fixes for selection, album handling, and Linux AppImage compatibility.

## Highlights

- **Map View** — Explore geotagged photos and videos on an interactive map directly from the main toolbar. The map follows your current view and filters, groups nearby items into clusters with photo counts, and lets you open a cluster to browse its photos. Return to the map without losing your position or zoom. (#223)
- **Google Motion Photos** — Play the embedded video in supported Google/Android Motion Photo JPEGs instead of seeing only the still image. Motion Photos are recognized in existing libraries and appear alongside Apple Live Photos through the unified Live & Motion Photos Smart Album condition. (#18)
- **Import and Organize by Date** — Import photos and videos from a folder into an album, automatically organizing them by day, month, year, or a single des

releases.name: v0.3.1
releases.body:
Lap v0.3.1 focuses on faster, safer library organization and a more capable review workflow. It adds folder search and inline folder creation, improves duplicate and related-photo review, makes album scanning clearer, and strengthens preview, thumbnail, and AI-search reliability across more formats and platforms.

## Highlights

- Folder Search — Search folders directly from the Albums sidebar. Matching folders remain in their album tree with clear highlighting, root-folder context, and favorite-folder filtering. (#260)
- Improved Duplicate Review — Duplicates and Similar Photos now support keep/unkeep actions, selected-item deletion, refresh and reanalyze controls, and more predictable group navigation.
- Related Photo Grouping — Configure a dedicated grouping strictness for Similar Photos, independent of the Find Similar Photos search setting. Exact duplicates are excluded from related-photo analysis.
- Safer Album Management — Album removal now cancels active indexing and waits for folder synchronization, preventing file-database errors during removal.
- Clearer Scan Progress — Album scans now report global progress through discovery, thumbnail generation, and search-dat

aiSummary.oneLiner: An open-source, privacy-first local photo manager for macOS, Windows, and Linux desktops.
aiSummary.whatItDoes: Lap is a cross-platform desktop application designed for organizing and viewing large local photo collections without relying on cloud services. It focuses on privacy and performance, ensuring that media metadata and indexing occur entirely on the user's machine. The application provides a clean, modern interface for browsing directories, filtering by dates, and viewing images. It serves as a lightweight alternative to bloated proprietary photo software, prioritizing speed and local control over data.
keyFeatures: Local processing: Keeps all image data, thumbnails, and metadata strictly on the local machine for complete privacy.
Cross-platform support: Provides a consistent user experience across Windows, macOS, and Linux operating systems.
Modern interface: Features a clean, responsive design for smooth scrolling and viewing of large media libraries.
Format compatibility: Supports a wide range of standard image formats commonly used by digital cameras and smartphones.
Open source: Allows community auditing of the code to guarantee no hidden telemetry or cloud syncing occurs.

useCases.title: Private Photo Archiving
useCases.description: Organize family photos on a local hard drive with the assurance that no data is being analyzed or uploaded to the cloud.

useCases.title: Cross-OS Media Management
useCases.description: Maintain a consistent photo viewing experience when switching between Linux workstations and Windows laptops.

useCases.title: Lightweight Browsing
useCases.description: Quickly scan through directories of raw images without the overhead of importing them into a heavy database.

useCases.title: Metadata Inspection
useCases.description: Examine EXIF data and shot details without exposing the information to third-party tracking services.

aiSummary.whoIsItFor: Privacy-conscious users, photographers, and anyone looking for a simple, fast local photo viewer. No technical skills required.
